h: Football Heritage and the South Side
p: Rutherglen is one of Scotland's ancient royal burghs, with a long and proud history of its own. Its Main Street has a proper town feel, with shops and cafés, and the old Rutherglen Town Hall is an impressive landmark.

Football fans have a treat just round the corner. Hampden Park, Scotland's national stadium, is only a short drive west in Mount Florida, and it's home to the Scottish Football Museum, packed with trophies, shirts and stories from the history of the game. A stadium tour is a great add-on for young fans.

If you've got time to head across the city, two of Glasgow's best family attractions are free. Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, in the west end, has everything from a Spitfire to stuffed animals, while the Riverside Museum, on the Clyde, is a transport museum with old trams, cars and a recreated street from the past, plus the tall ship Glenlee moored outside.
For a nature fix south of the city, Calderglen Country Park in East Kilbride has woodland walks, a children's zoo and a big adventure play area.

The south side of Glasgow is well served by trains and buses, and with the M74 so close, it's straightforward to reach by car. That makes it a good choice for families from across Lanarkshire as well as the city.
On wet days, which Glasgow is not short of, a bounce plus a free museum is a cracking combination.
